summary:
Podcast show notes for Episode 408 of Eptura's Workplace Innovator, hosted by Mike Petrusky, featuring Kevin Sauer, MCR.w, Head of US Operations and Client Delivery at Nhance.ai (a digital twin and smart building platform) and Founder and CEO of Sauer Strategy Works, LLC. Sauer's consulting focus is workforce and workplace strategy, technology and tool selection, and change management programs.

The conversation centers on the theme "Be More Human": Sauer argues human connection remains central to innovation, and that engagement with colleagues, leaders and outside perspectives is essential to the future of workplace strategy. The notes state that the COVID-19 pandemic accelerated acceptance and implementation of flexible workplace strategies including activity-based working and shared desking.

Sauer also predicts AI and robotics will significantly impact the workplace and facilities industry, spanning automation of administrative tasks through optimization of facility operations. The recommended response for workplace and facility leaders is to focus on upskilling, to embrace both human and technological intelligence, and to maintain a holistic view of the built environment. Mike and Kevin reportedly share practical case studies and inspiration for listeners.

The remainder of the item is promotional links: Sauer's LinkedIn and consulting site, the YouTube playlist, the Workplace Innovator archive of free resources and past interviews, Eptura's site, and Petrusky's LinkedIn. No statistics, survey data, customer counts or named case study details appear in the text itself, so the item functions as an episode teaser rather than a substantive analysis. Shared desking is mentioned only in passing as a pandemic-accelerated flexible strategy, without discussion of employee reaction or effectiveness.

claims.claim: The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated acceptance and implementation of flexible workplace strategies such as activity-based working and shared desking.
AI and robotics are poised to significantly impact the workplace industry, from automating administrative tasks to optimizing facility operations.
Human connection remains central to innovation, and engagement with colleagues, leaders and outside perspectives is essential to future workplace strategy.
Workplace and facility leaders should focus on upskilling and maintain a holistic view of the built environment.
